these are entities to which we want customers to attach their Azure resources to, right? Then lets maybe add the azureResource signal group as a "commented-out template"

And maybe add that to the display name? "Database (attach CosmosDB here)"?

use computeEntity.Name
a) it doesnt drift
b) adds an implicit dependsOn which might be helpful here (same for any other discovery rules in your examples which tie to an existing entity)

Internally we use GUIDs for relationship names and they support a properties.displayName attribute. In the interest of showing best practices here we should make do it here as well. @sebader thoughts?
I would say its fine to use speaking names here. Using Guids isn't really a best practice, at least in IaC scenarios, I would say.
Or as an alternative maybe `${parent.name}-${child.name}` if we don't want to use GUIDs here.

this must be idempotent and unique to the tenant...  use:
```
name: guid(backupVault.id, roleDefinitionId, storageAccount.id)
```
Note the last part (storageAccount.id) will depend on the scope of the roleAssignment.
